Its lone-pair interaction can nevertheless influence the relative stabilisation of intermediates for attack at different positions, favouring ortho and para relative to meta. Deactivation compares the substituted ring with benzene, whereas orientation compares competing positions within that substituted ring. These are different comparisons, so the stated combination is consistent.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) applies an exceptionless rule that fails for halogens. (C) treats one net kinetic observation as proof that a competing electronic effect is absent. (D) equates positional direction with overall activation.

syllabus_anchor: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: preparation of ethers; Williamson synthesis
reasoning_focus: A Williamson target has one suitable reagent orientation and one invalid aryl-SN2 reversal
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Two Williamson routes are proposed for phenetole, Ph–O–CH2CH3, under ordinary SN2 conditions: P uses sodium phenoxide and bromoethane; Q uses sodium ethoxide and bromobenzene. Which assessment is correct?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Williamson synthesis requires a suitable substitution centre. Bromoethane offers a primary sp3 carbon at which phenoxide can displace bromide. Reversing the partners leaves bromine on an aromatic sp2 carbon; ordinary backside SN2 substitution at that aryl centre is not the corresponding viable process. Atom balance is necessary for a synthetic proposal but does not establish the required mechanism.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) ignores which atom bears the leaving group. (B) reverses the usual substrate suitability. (D) denies the nucleophilic role of alkoxide or phenoxide oxygen.

syllabus_anchor: Aldehydes and Ketones: oxidative cleavage; carbon-skeleton accounting
reasoning_focus: Carbonyl-carbon isotope retention resolves an otherwise ambiguous oxidative acid-fragment pair
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Pentan-2-one and pentan-3-one are candidates for an unknown ketone. Under the specified oxidative-cleavage conditions both candidates can give one ethanoic-acid and one propanoic-acid fragment. The original carbonyl carbon is 13C-labelled, remains in one acid's carboxyl group, and no carbon scrambling occurs. The label is found in ethanoic acid. Which inference follows?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: The supplied label tracks the original carbonyl carbon through a carbon-conserving cleavage. Without that tracking, the same pair of unlabelled fragment formulas would not distinguish the candidates under the stated conditions. No universal regioselectivity beyond the supplied cleavage model is assumed.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) gives pentan-3-one a methyl neighbour it does not possess. (B) ignores the conserved total of two plus three carbons. (C) discards the stated ambiguity that the isotope experiment resolves.

syllabus_anchor: Amines: diazotisation; replacement of diazonium group by hydrogen
reasoning_focus: A temporary amino directing group establishes an alternating bromine pattern before reductive removal
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Aniline is brominated with excess bromine water to give the usual 2,4,6-tribromo derivative. Its amino group is then diazotised at 0–5 degrees C and replaced by hydrogen using H3PO2, with the bromines retained. Which final aromatic product is obtained after renumbering the ring?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: A temporary directing group can establish a substitution pattern and then be removed; replacing the group does not move the other substituents.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) stops before diazotisation and deamination. (C) uses the hydrolysis product associated with water rather than the supplied reducing reagent. (D) removes two bromines without a stipulated reaction.

syllabus_anchor: Solutions: Raoult's law; vapour-pressure lowering
reasoning_focus: A second nonvolatile solute changes the full solvent mole-fraction denominator
object_constraints_and_requested_result: One mole of solvent is mixed ideally with 0.10 mol nonvolatile solute X and 0.15 mol nonvolatile solute Y. Neither associates nor dissociates. What is the final solvent vapour pressure divided by its pure vapour pressure, and why is it not 1/1.10?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: For an ideal solution with nonvolatile solutes, \(p_{solvent}=x_{solvent}p^0\).
distractor_mechanisms: (A) neglects Y and also approximates the remaining ratio incorrectly. (C) subtracts amounts without dividing by total moles. (D) inverts the mole-fraction ratio.

syllabus_anchor: Electrochemistry: electrode potentials; Gibbs energy and cell emf
reasoning_focus: Electron-weighted Gibbs-energy addition combines unequal-electron reduction steps
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Standard reduction potentials are A3+ + e− → A2+, E1°=+0.50 V, and A2+ + 2e− → A(s), E2°=-0.10 V. What is E° for A3+ + 3e− → A(s), and its standard Gibbs energy change expressed using Faraday constant F?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Gibbs energies are additive; potentials themselves are not extensive.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) directly adds potentials. (B) takes an unweighted arithmetic mean. (D) reverses the sign of the final reduction.

syllabus_anchor: Chemical Kinetics: rate law; pseudo-first-order reactions
reasoning_focus: Excess-reactant control changes the observed order and slope without changing the intrinsic law
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A reaction has intrinsic rate law r=k[A][B]. In two runs B is maintained in large excess so its concentration changes negligibly. Run P uses [B]=0.20 M and run Q uses [B]=0.40 M. What logarithmic A-time behaviour and interpretation follow?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: The controlled concentration becomes part of the observed coefficient. A first-order trace in one monitored reactant is not proof that the intrinsic law contains only that reactant.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) ignores the excess-reactant approximation. (B) confuses constant intrinsic k with the concentration-dependent observed coefficient. (C) assigns an order from amount alone.

syllabus_anchor: Thermodynamics: calorimetry; Hess's law; enthalpy of ionisation
reasoning_focus: A matched dilution blank changes the inferred weak-acid ionisation enthalpy
object_constraints_and_requested_result: At the same temperature, neutralising 0.100 mol strong acid with strong base releases 5.70 kJ. Neutralising 0.100 mol weak monoprotic acid HA with the same base releases 5.20 kJ as measured. A matched dilution blank for the weak-acid run releases 0.20 kJ and is included in that measured heat. What molar enthalpy of HA ionisation follows? Assume the remaining reaction steps are identical.
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Hess's law compares the weak-acid reaction with the strong-ion neutralisation after subtracting the blank.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) omits the dilution correction. (C) reverses the enthalpy sign. (D) fails to convert the 0.100 mol heat difference to a per-mole value.

syllabus_anchor: Equilibrium: heterogeneous equilibria; reaction quotient; material balance
reasoning_focus: Solid-phase exhaustion limits equilibrium gas pressure in one of two otherwise identical vessels
object_constraints_and_requested_result: For CaCO3(s) ⇌ CaO(s)+CO2(g), Kp=0.40 bar at a fixed temperature. Two identical rigid vessels have RT/V=1.00 bar mol−1 and initially contain no CO2 but 0.50 mol CaO. P contains 1.00 mol CaCO3; Q contains only 0.10 mol CaCO3. What are the final CO2 pressures, allowing a solid phase to be exhausted?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: The Kp pressure condition for the displayed heterogeneous equilibrium requires both solid phases to remain available.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) ignores Q's limiting carbonate amount. (C) equates all P carbonate with obligatory decomposition despite equilibrium. (D) reverses the inventories.

syllabus_anchor: The d- and f-Block Elements: lanthanoids; actinoids; oxidation states
reasoning_focus: Formal f-electron accounting linked to lanthanoid exceptions and actinoid oxidation-state variation
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Use the neutral configurations Ce: [Xe]4f1 5d1 6s2, Eu: [Xe]4f7 6s2 and U: [Rn]5f3 6d1 7s2. In the usual formal valence-electron accounting for Ce4+, Eu2+ and U6+, which f counts and interpretation are consistent?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: The dominant +3 tendency of lanthanoids does not prohibit particular +2 or +4 states. Empty or half-filled configurations contribute to some exceptions, while participation of nearby-energy actinoid orbitals allows a wider range of oxidation states. This is not a prediction that every formally writable ion is equally stable in every medium.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) stops removing electrons despite the required charges. (B) has the counts but replaces orbital energetics with an unsupported mass rule. (D) gives cations extra electrons instead of removing them.

syllabus_anchor: Matrices and Determinants: matrix multiplication; polynomial identities; determinants
reasoning_focus: Concrete matrix identity reduces a high-degree polynomial to a linear matrix expression
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Let \(A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-2&3\end{pmatrix}\), which satisfies A²-3A+2I=0. Find \(\det(A^5-3A^4+4A^2-I)\).
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Multiply the identity by powers of A and combine like matrix terms before taking a determinant.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) loses the determinant sign. (C) uses only one diagonal entry. (D) confuses a scalar multiple or trace with the determinant.

syllabus_anchor: Permutations and Combinations: repeated objects; restrictions
reasoning_focus: Repeated intact blocks and disjoint endpoint cases in a multiset arrangement
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Five tiles consist of two identical tiles marked AB, two identical tiles marked C and one tile marked D. Tiles remain intact in a row. How many distinct rows have D at either end?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Count the endpoint cases and divide by factorials for repeated units.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) counts only one end. (B) divides by only one repeated-pair factorial after selecting the endpoint. (C) counts unrestricted positions of D.

syllabus_anchor: Relations and Functions: composition; onto functions; finite maps
reasoning_focus: An onto composition constrains the final factor but leaves an unused intermediate element
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Let f:{1,2,3}→{a,b,c,d} map 1,2,3 to a,b,c respectively. How many maps g:{a,b,c,d}→{0,1} make g∘f onto {0,1}, and what does this require of f and g?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: An onto composition must attain both final outputs on the image of f.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) reverses the necessary implication. (C) subtracts too few constant-on-image assignments and misstates f's property. (D) omits the choice at d and contradicts g's forced surjectivity.

syllabus_anchor: Complex Numbers: conjugates; Quadratic and Polynomial Equations: roots and coefficients
reasoning_focus: Conjugate pairing and cubic root product determine a real but negative square sum
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A real-coefficient cubic is x³+ax²+bx-10 and has root 1+2i. What is the sum of the squares of all three roots, counting multiplicity?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Use conjugacy and the root product, then compute complex squares rather than squared moduli.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) loses the negative real contribution. (B) uses an unrelated root product. (D) sums squared moduli, 5+5+4, rather than the requested complex squares.

syllabus_anchor: Integral Calculus: piecewise definite integrals; areas
reasoning_focus: A minimum of two curves and an absolute value require two different sets of breakpoints
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2}\left|\min\{x^2,2-x^2\}\right|\,dx\).
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Locate crossings before applying the absolute value; exploit even symmetry only after identifying the pieces.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) evaluates the signed integral without the absolute value. (B) counts only the positive half-axis. (C) loses the constant endpoint contributions.

syllabus_anchor: Three-dimensional Geometry: vector equations of lines; parallel and coincident lines
reasoning_focus: A direction parameter gives parallelism while an independent base-point parameter gives coincidence
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Lines L1=(1,0,2)+t(1,2,-1) and L2=(b,2,1)+s(2,k,-2) depend on real b,k. Which pair makes them the same line, rather than merely parallel?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Compare direction ratios first, then check the displacement between base points.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) gives parallel but displaced lines. (C) fails the direction ratio. (D) gives an inconsistent y-direction sign.

syllabus_anchor: Differentiation: implicit functions; tangent interpretation
reasoning_focus: An indeterminate implicit derivative is resolved through two explicit branches with a shared tangent
object_constraints_and_requested_result: For the real curve y²=x⁴, the formula y'=2x³/y gives 0/0 at the origin. What are the tangent lines there when both real branches are considered?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Factor the defining equation into its real branches.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) interprets division by zero as an infinite slope without checking the numerator. (C) assigns slopes not obtained from either branch. (D) contradicts direct substitution.

syllabus_anchor: Statistics: mean; population variance; affine changes
reasoning_focus: Pairing observations with affine reflections changes a pooled variance through mean separation
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A data set has n observations, mean 2 and population variance 3. A new set of 2n observations contains every original x once and its reflected value 8-x once. What are the new mean and population variance?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Compute paired deviations about the new mean, including the separation of the two group means.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) omits group separation. (B) treats reflection as unchanged duplication. (D) uses only the reflected group's mean.

syllabus_anchor: Limits and Continuity: standard limits; inequalities; functions
reasoning_focus: A floor-function squeeze controls a trigonometric quotient at infinity
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Let ⌊x⌋ be the greatest integer not exceeding x. Find \(\displaystyle\lim_{x\to+\infty}x\sin\frac1{\lfloor x\rfloor}\).
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Bound the real-to-integer ratio, then use the standard sine limit.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) keeps the small sine factor but ignores the growing x factor. (B) infers failure from jumps without the squeeze estimate. (C) uses an incorrect limiting ratio x/n.

syllabus_anchor: Probability: Bayes's theorem; conditional probability; sampling bias
reasoning_focus: Different sampling protocols produce different conditional box probabilities from identical contents
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Box A contains one red and one blue ball; box B contains three red and one blue. In protocol P, choose a box with probability 1/2 each and then choose a ball uniformly from it. In protocol Q, choose uniformly from all six balls while retaining each ball's box label. Given a red ball, what are P(B|red) in protocols P and Q, respectively?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Apply Bayes's rule using the actual sampling mechanism.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) exchanges protocols. (C) ignores the red observation and the unequal box-size weighting. (D) updates P but not Q.

syllabus_anchor: Trigonometric Functions: identities; inequalities; periodicity
reasoning_focus: A squared trigonometric factor splits connected solution bands without changing sign
object_constraints_and_requested_result: For 0≤x≤5π/2, consider sin(2x)cos x>0. How many connected solution intervals are there, and what is their total length?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Factor before constructing the sign chart, retaining zeros even when a squared factor does not change sign.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) ignores the interior zero that splits a band. (C) counts regions where sin x is negative. (D) omits the last positive partial period.

syllabus_anchor: Differential Equations: linear equations; Applications of Derivatives: extrema
reasoning_focus: A singular linear initial-value equation requires a component-specific global minimum
object_constraints_and_requested_result: The solution of \(y'+2y/(x-1)=1/(x-1)^2\), y(0)=1, is taken on its maximal real interval containing zero. What are that interval and the minimum value of y there?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Solve with an integrating factor on the initial point's component, then minimise only on that component.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) crosses the forbidden singularity. (B) overlooks negative values and the stationary minimum. (D) chooses the component not containing the initial point.

syllabus_anchor: Quadratic Equations: discriminant; roots and coefficients; inequalities
reasoning_focus: Real-root discriminant and strict product positivity yield disconnected parameter intervals
object_constraints_and_requested_result: For which real a does \(x^2-(a+1)x+2a-1=0\) have real roots, not necessarily distinct, whose product is positive?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Combine discriminant nonnegativity with Vieta's root-product condition.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) uses the negative-discriminant region. (C) ignores the discriminant gap. (D) omits the positive-product restriction.

syllabus_anchor: Coordinate Geometry: straight lines; distance; orthogonal coordinates
reasoning_focus: An orthonormal change of coordinates converts a line equation without changing distance
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Define rotated coordinates u=(3x+4y)/5 and v=(-4x+3y)/5. Which equation describes the line 3x+4y=10 in these coordinates, and what is its perpendicular distance from the origin?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: An orthogonal rotation preserves lengths; alternatively use the original point-line distance formula.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) exchanges the rotated axes. (B) omits the factor 5 in both equation and distance. (C) transforms the equation but fails to normalise the distance.

syllabus_anchor: Vector Algebra: cross and dot products; Three-dimensional Geometry: plane distance
reasoning_focus: An ordered triangle fixes the sign of a plane normal and a signed projection
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A plane is oriented by the ordered points A=(1,0,0), B=(0,1,0), C=(0,0,1), with unit normal along AB×AC. For P=(1,1,1), which normal and signed perpendicular displacement from the plane are correct?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Normalise AB×AC and project P-A onto that unit normal.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) gives a sign inconsistent with its normal. (B) reverses the prescribed orientation without changing the projected sign accordingly. (D) uses a nonunit normal as if it measured perpendicular distance.

syllabus_anchor: Motion in a Straight Line: velocity-time graph; displacement; distance
reasoning_focus: A continuous piecewise velocity returns to its start after two reversals but travels a nonzero path
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A particle's velocity graph is v=t-1 m s−1 for 0≤t≤2 s and v=3-t m s−1 for 2≤t≤4 s, with t entered in seconds. What are its displacement and total distance over these four seconds?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Displacement is signed area under v(t); distance is area under |v(t)|.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) treats signed cancellation as zero distance. (C) uses unsigned area for displacement. (D) uses rectangular rather than triangular areas.

syllabus_anchor: Laws of Motion: vertical circular motion; Work and Energy: conservation
reasoning_focus: A rope-strength limit must be applied at the global maximum tension, with a separate tautness check
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A mass m on a light inextensible rope of length L moves in a vertical circle under gravity alone apart from rope tension. At a point 60 degrees from the downward vertical its speed is v. The rope breaks if tension exceeds 8mg. What is the greatest v compatible with completing the circle without breaking the rope anywhere?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Use energy to connect the stated point to the bottom, where tension is largest.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) applies the breaking limit locally at 60 degrees only. (B) omits the gravitational tension contribution. (D) is smaller than the permitted maximum.

syllabus_anchor: Work, Energy and Power: conservative and nonconservative work
reasoning_focus: Closed-path work fixes total dissipation but only bounds an individual potential difference
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A body is moved quasistatically from A to B along one rough path with external work +10 J, then from B to A along another rough path with external work -4 J. It returns to the same mechanical state, all friction is dissipative, and the only stored-energy change on an individual leg is a conservative potential U. What are total dissipated heat and the possible range of UB-UA?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: External work equals stored-potential increase plus dissipative loss.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) adds work magnitudes instead of signed work. (C) mistakes cycle dissipation for a one-leg potential difference. (D) treats a return to the same state as zero dissipated energy.

syllabus_anchor: System of Particles and Rotational Motion: rolling; torque; friction
reasoning_focus: An axle torque requires uphill static friction to couple rotation to uphill translation
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A uniform solid cylinder of mass M and radius R rolls without slipping up a 30-degree incline. A pure external torque MgR is applied in the rotation direction for uphill rolling and exerts no net force. Use ICM=MR²/2 and assume enough static friction. What are its centre acceleration and friction force?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Couple centre-of-mass force balance to torque balance and the rolling constraint.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) omits rotational inertia and gives the wrong friction direction. (B) reverses friction and violates translation balance. (C) does not satisfy the two equations simultaneously.

syllabus_anchor: Gravitation: escape speed; satellite motion; kinetic energy
reasoning_focus: Radial and prograde impulses reach the same escape energy through different vector additions
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A satellite initially has circular speed vc=√(GM/r) at radius r. A short impulse adds a velocity increment either radially outward or in the original tangential direction. Neglect displacement during the impulse. What are the minimum increment magnitudes for escape in these two cases, respectively?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Escape requires final speed at least √2 vc; add velocities vectorially before evaluating kinetic energy.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) reverses the geometries. (C) reports the required total speed as the added speed. (D) satisfies neither threshold.

syllabus_anchor: Mechanical Properties of Fluids: surface tension; surface energy
reasoning_focus: Soap-film work counts two interfaces rather than one projected rectangle
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A soap film spans a frame with a movable side of length 0.10 m. It is extended quasistatically by 0.020 m at constant surface tension 0.030 N m−1. Ignore gravity and other forces. What is the work and its ratio to making the same area increase at one liquid–air interface?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Surface-creation work is γ times the total increase in interfacial area.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) counts only one face. (B) calculates two faces but gives a one-face ratio. (D) counts the two-surface factor twice.

syllabus_anchor: Thermodynamics: ideal-gas processes; first law; quasistatic work
reasoning_focus: A specified power-law compression heats the gas while releasing heat
object_constraints_and_requested_result: One mole of monatomic ideal gas is compressed quasistatically along PV^(3/2)=constant from V0 to V0/4, starting at temperature T0. Use Cv=3R/2 and the convention ΔU=Q-Wby. What heat Q enters the gas?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Obtain final temperature from the path and ideal-gas law; integrate P dV for work.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) reverses heat direction. (C) identifies heat with internal-energy change and omits work. (D) assumes every power-law compression is adiabatic.

syllabus_anchor: Electric Charges and Fields: Gauss's law; conductors; Electrostatic Potential: work
reasoning_focus: Equal exterior charge data conceal different interior field work for conducting and volume-charged spheres
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Two spheres of radius R each carry total positive charge Q. One is a nonconducting sphere with uniform volume charge; the other is a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium. A small positive test charge q is moved quasistatically from the surface to the centre without changing the distributions. What work is done by the electric field in the two cases, respectively?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Apply Gauss's law inside each sphere, then integrate field work along the inward path.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) reverses the inward-work sign. (B) exchanges the materials. (C) treats interior work as if both had a central point charge.

syllabus_anchor: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance: dielectrics; parallel capacitors; stored energy
reasoning_focus: Partial dielectric overlap creates a fixed-charge energy gradient and inward force
object_constraints_and_requested_result: An isolated parallel-plate capacitor initially has capacitance C0=ε0 bL/d and fixed charge Q. A dielectric of relative permittivity 3 fills the full gap over width b and inserted length x, leaving the remaining plate length L-x empty. Use the parallel-area capacitance approximation, neglecting fringing corrections to C. What is the dielectric's force magnitude at x=L/2, and its direction?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Add their capacitances in parallel and use F=-dU/dx with U=Q²/(2C).
distractor_mechanisms: (A) uses the zero-insertion magnitude and wrong direction. (C) loses a factor two. (D) confuses isolation with absence of stored energy.

syllabus_anchor: Moving Charges and Magnetism: velocity selector; motion in a magnetic field
reasoning_focus: A velocity selector fixes equal speeds before mass-to-charge and energy ratios are compared
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Two positive ion beams have masses and charges (m,q) and (4m,2q). They pass undeflected through the same crossed-field velocity selector, then enter the same uniform magnetic analyser perpendicular to its field. What are the second beam's radius divided by the first's, and its kinetic energy divided by the first's?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Balance qE=qvB in the selector, then use r=mv/(qBa) in the analyser.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) ignores mass-to-charge differences in radius. (B) uses a same-accelerating-voltage rule instead of velocity selection. (D) ignores the second beam's doubled charge in the radius.

syllabus_anchor: Electromagnetic Induction: magnetic flux; motional emf
reasoning_focus: Translation changes flux only while loop overlap with a bounded field changes
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A square conducting loop of side a moves right at speed v through a stationary field stripe of width 3a, whose magnetic field points into the page. At t=0 its leading edge reaches the stripe's left boundary. Neglect self-inductance. During which open time interval is the induced current zero while the loop is wholly within the field?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Induced emf is minus the rate of change of magnetic flux through the moving loop.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) is the growing-overlap entry interval. (C) is the shrinking-overlap exit interval. (D) substitutes velocity for flux change.

syllabus_anchor: Ray Optics: refraction at a prism; total internal reflection; critical angle
reasoning_focus: Changing the surrounding medium removes total internal reflection without changing internal ray geometry
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A right-angled isosceles glass prism has refractive index √3. A ray enters normally through a short face and reaches the hypotenuse at internal incidence 45 degrees. Compare the exit at that face when the surrounding medium is air and when the whole prism is immersed in transparent liquid of index 4/3. Which result follows?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: At the exit, Snell law requires \(n_g\sin i=n_{out}\sin r\); transmission requires the computed sine not exceed one.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) ignores the changed outside index. (C) accepts a sine exceeding one. (D) fails to divide by the liquid index.

syllabus_anchor: Wave Optics: coherence; interference; addition of waves
reasoning_focus: Time-averaged phase switching removes contrast unlike a constant phase offset
object_constraints_and_requested_result: Two equal coherent slit contributions have individual intensity I0. In P their phase is stable. In Q an extra phase alternates rapidly between 0 and π for equal times, and the detector averages over many switches. What are Q's mean intensities at P's bright and dark positions, and how would a constant extra π phase differ?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Equal coherent contributions give intensity \(2I_0[1+\cos\delta]\); average intensities over the specified phase states.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) omits switching and misstates a fixed-phase effect. (B) describes one phase state rather than the average. (C) violates the summed background intensity and invents a wavelength change.

syllabus_anchor: Atoms: Bohr model; de Broglie's quantisation explanation
reasoning_focus: Orbit circumference and matter wavelength jointly determine ionic charge and level energy
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A hydrogen-like one-electron ion has orbit radius 2a0 and electron de Broglie wavelength πa0, where a0 is the hydrogen ground-state Bohr radius. Use 2πr=nλ, r=a0 n²/Z and En=-13.6 Z²/n² eV. Which n,Z and energy fit all three conditions?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Apply the orbit standing-wave condition before the radius and energy relations.
distractor_mechanisms: (A) violates the circumference count. (B) uses the right n but fails the radius. (C) doubles n despite the measured wavelength.

syllabus_anchor: Nuclei: radioactive decay law and half-life; statistical nature of nuclear decay
reasoning_focus: Conditional survival distinguishes a statistical half-life from an individual nuclear lifetime
object_constraints_and_requested_result: A radioactive nuclide obeys exponential decay with half-life T. One nucleus has already survived for 3T; another nucleus of the same nuclide has just been produced. Their environments are identical. What are their respective probabilities of surviving the next interval T, and can their past histories fix which one decays first?
governing_method_or_causal_mechanism: Condition on the fact that the older nucleus is still present; do not count its earlier survival twice.
distractor_mechanisms: (B) uses the unconditional probability of surviving all four half-lives instead of conditioning on the first three already survived. (C) invents an initial interval during which decay is impossible. (D) treats three half-lives as an individual lifetime limit despite the nonzero exponential survival probability.
